push_headlines: Asian chipmakers rallied on Jensen Huang's return: the Nikkei 225 +3.91% to 58,644.63 and the Kospi +6.98% back above 5,000.
Europe gave back some of Monday's rebound: the STOXX 600 -0.66% to 632.74 as ASML slipped.
Oil kept sliding on US-Iran talk hopes: Brent near $89.08 (-0.32%), about 24% below its October 30 close.
on_notice: Wall Street split Tuesday, with the Dow +0.85% to close above 50,000 while tech lagged; watch whether Asia's chip rally holds tonight.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng -0.73% to an 18-month low even as Seoul and Tokyo surged; China remains the weak spot in the region.
Brent is down about 24% from $117.64 on October 30 ahead of the OPEC+ meeting on November 29; any US-Iran deal headline could move it sharply.

asia.headline: Tokyo and Seoul surged as chip suppliers rallied on Nvidia's leadership news.
asia.detail: The Nikkei 225 +3.91% to 58,644.63 as Tokyo caught up after Monday's holiday (other reports put the gain near +4.11%). The Kospi +6.98% to 5,036.99, recovering from Monday's 4,708.54 (a single report; treat as provisional), and Taiwan's Taiex also posted a large gain.

china.headline: Hong Kong slipped to an 18-month low as early AI gains faded.
china.detail: The Hang Seng -0.73% to 22,219.65 and the Hang Seng Tech Index -1.17% to 3,466, with Xiaomi and Meituan both down more than 3%. No verified Shanghai Composite close was found, so none is quoted here.

europe.headline: European stocks eased as Monday's tech rally faded.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 -0.66% to 632.74, giving back part of Monday's rebound, with ASML -3.45% in US trading. No verified DAX or FTSE 100 close was found, so none is quoted here.

latam.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa fell again as Vale and Petrobras weighed.
latam.detail: The Ibovespa -0.43% to 164,089.81 after trading as high as 167,580 intraday; Vale -5.51% and CSN -6.90% as commodities came under pressure, and Petrobras's chief gave no promise of extraordinary dividends. The dollar eased to about R$5.91.

mideast.headline: Oil drifted lower as markets weighed a possible US-Iran agreement.
mideast.detail: January Brent $89.08 (-0.32%) at 15:58 GMT, about 24% below its October 30 close of $117.64, ahead of the OPEC+ meeting on November 29. WTI traded near $79.79. No settlement price was found.
